Trigger: start a TUI mutation; send SIGINT; send a second SIGINT during Close. Outcome: process dies; CLI never prints the independent session receipt; closeOwner may not run. tui_process_linux_test.go only sends one signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the process interrupt handler armed until session.Close returns (or ignore SIGINT during Close after the first cancel), then Stop. Assumption: cooperative cleanup should finish before default termination.
findings.title: Second SIGINT kills Close before session receipt
findings.why_it_matters: After the first interrupt, default SIGINT is restored while session.Close still waits on in-flight work, so a second interrupt can abort closeOwner and skip publishing HadCommittedChanges/OutcomeUnknown after a committed or unknown write.

residual_risks: Owned Kitty inspection is not substituted by Linux PTY tests that set TERM=xterm-kitty; restoration sequences in a PTY slave are not Kitty window/terminal-restoration evidence.

Storage treats a known commit as success even if cancellation follows it (internal/storage/transaction.go:154); TUI Session only sets HadCommittedChanges when err == nil. Injected after-commit TransactionError paths are not the production service return.
Recovery Acknowledge / discard intentionally drops the form after an unknown write (anti-replay). If the write did not land, the user must re-enter the draft from the recovery screen copy.
Cross-compiled TUI/CLI test binaries in Makefile are compile-only; they are not native runtime verification.
